themes_detail.label: Damaged Street Signs Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage complaints surged to 6 THIS WEEK compared to a 1.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 243% spike (z-score: 3.9)—suggesting possible weather damage, vehicle collisions, or infrastructure deterioration requiring immediate public safety review.
evidence: 6 street sign damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (243% increase, z-score: 3.9)
Statistically significant spike with high severity classification
Timing suggests possible acute event (weather, accidents, or systematic deterioration)
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent weather events (wind, rain) caused the spike or if there's an underlying infrastructure maintenance gap
Interview DOT about inspection protocols and repair timelines for damaged street signs in CD 411

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK versus a 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69, highest severity)—suggesting possible HVAC failures, mold, or ventilation crises in residential or commercial buildings.
evidence: 3 indoor air quality complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69)
Highest z-score among all spikes, indicating extreme statistical anomaly
Health-critical issue affecting indoor environments where residents spend most time
reporting_angles: Track specific addresses and building types: are complaints concentrated in older buildings, schools, community centers, or residential units?
Interview affected residents about symptoms and request NYC DEP or DOHMH data on any environmental investigations in the area

themes_detail.label: Hazardous Materials Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Hazardous materials complaints peaked at 5 THREE WEEKS AGO (compared to 0.4 weekly average)—a 1233% spike (z-score: 9.55, highest severity)—indicating possible chemical spill, industrial discharge, or contamination event requiring environmental investigation.
evidence: 5 hazardous materials complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1233% increase, z-score: 9.55)
Second-highest z-score, indicating extreme statistical anomaly with severe classification
Suggests acute incident (spill, discharge, or contamination) rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Obtain 311 complaint details (addresses, substance descriptions) and cross-reference with EPA, FDNY HAZMAT, or DEP incident reports from 3 weeks ago
Contact FDNY to determine if any hazmat incidents, chemical spills, or facility contamination was documented in that period

themes_detail.label: Obstruction Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints rose to 13 LAST WEEK versus a 3.9 weekly average—a 236% spike (z-score: 5.94)—suggesting possible illegal sidewalk blockages, construction debris, or encroachments affecting pedestrian access across the district.
evidence: 13 obstruction complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (236% increase, z-score: 5.94)
High z-score with high severity rating
Directly impacts pedestrian accessibility and public right-of-way
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify whether obstructions cluster around specific areas (construction sites, parks, commercial corridors)
Interview DOT and SCA about active construction permits or street work that may have triggered blockages

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Tree Complaints Rise
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints doubled to 16 LAST WEEK from a 7.6 weekly baseline—a 110% spike (z-score: 3.66)—potentially linked to recent weather stress, disease, or deferred Parks Department maintenance in this district.
evidence: 16 dead/dying tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 7.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (110% increase, z-score: 3.66)
Aligns with CB 411's recurring budget requests for 'damaged tree' improvements and park/building access upgrades
Suggests systemic underinvestment in tree care matching historical CB funding priorities
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Parks about tree inspection and removal backlogs in CD 411; ask whether recent weather (wind, drought stress) is a factor
Cross-reference with 'Damaged Tree' complaints (221 total over 90 days) to assess whether tree health is a growing district-wide issue
